summary: The change passes. A request can now carry `Priority: high`, `normal` or `low` (any case) as a line in its words. A request with no such line is normal and keeps today's order. `athena plan` orders by dependencies first, then priority, then rung, then age. A high request's prerequisites inherit its priority, so they run before unrelated older work. That covers the cutover case, where the urgent request had a dependency. I ran `cargo test -p athena-core plan`: all 21 tests passed, including the new ones for ordering, dependencies, the default order and parsing. The targeted athena-cli tests for the plan and status output also passed. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and full test runs all passed. I found no blocker or major problems. The minor ones: two files outside the deliverables list (main.rs and drain.rs) changed, but only their help and doc text, and both were planned. `athena status` shows a priority only when it is high or low, so no label means normal; this is documented in D118 and the CHANGELOG.
